paths.description: Homepage and primary discovery listing; tested desktop, 360×800, preference media, performance, network, privacy, accessibility, discoverability, and memory.
Representative category/listing template; visually checked as a shared listing archetype.
Representative media detail/player route; checked desktop and narrow layout without starting playback.
Primary account-entry surface, inspected without submitting personal data.
Deliberate invalid route to inspect HTTP/navigation recovery state.

findings.summary: Theme does not follow the user’s light/dark preference.
findings.evidence: Paired light and dark captures are visually unchanged, and the DOM reports color-scheme: normal; the interface remains dark under prefers-color-scheme: light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and derive surfaces from prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), retaining the existing dark palette as one preference-aware option.

findings.summary: Loading shimmer continues under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found eight running shimmer animations, each 2000 ms, while matchMedia confirmed prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential shimmer animation inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), replacing it with a static loading treatment.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not handled and baseline contrast failures remain.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no prefers-contrast/forced-colors handling; Lighthouse reported color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, and correct the baseline failing color pairs.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The loaded CSS contained no view-transition usage; navigation is conventional full replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin route/state changes with View Transitions and preserve normal navigation as fallback.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation does not react to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The first viewport and feature probe show fixed dense chrome but no scroll-state/container-query or scroll-timeline treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent chrome as users scroll and expose a lightweight position/progress cue where useful.

findings.summary: Menus and transient controls do not use resilient CSS anchoring.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage despite multiple header dropdown controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions for dropdowns near viewport edges.

findings.summary: A large consent modal obscures every sampled primary surface on first load.
findings.evidence: Homepage, detail, search, and signup captures all show the same near-full-viewport consent interruption covering core content. Reject is available, but reading or acting requires clearing the overlay first.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface when legally permitted, retaining equally prominent accept/reject controls and accessible preference management.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay lacks dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: While the modal was visible, the feature probe found zero <dialog> elements and zero [role=dialog] elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, an accessible name, focus containment/restoration, and explicit close/choice actions.

findings.summary: Dense navigation and promotional chrome compete with primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and narrow captures devote a large persistent left rail plus multiple top promotional bands to chrome; the narrow view leaves only a small clipped content column.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation and promotions on narrow screens, prioritising the listing/player and one primary action.

findings.summary: The site serves a desktop-width layout at a 360 px visual viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout recorded scrollWidth 1038 versus visualViewportWidth 360, 678 px horizontal overflow, on both homepage and detail. The signup mobile capture places the form mostly off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed 1024 px page widths, size from the visual viewport, and reflow header/sidebar/content into a single narrow-screen layout.

findings.summary: Reused components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules, and the narrow screenshot shows desktop header/sidebar/content dimensions preserved and clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, navigation, search, and account panels containment and size-aware @container layouts with intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and many targets are too short.
findings.evidence: The first focused link computed to outline: none and box-shadow: none. The probe lists many 25–40 px-high controls; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clearly visible :focus-visible treatment and raise touch hit areas to at least 44 CSS px without relying on hover.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.4 s and FCP 2.8 s, while the desktop trace was faster at 1.14 s; the common mobile condition misses the 2.5 s good LCP threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP element and reduce blocking/unused work on mobile; validate with repeat mobile traces.

findings.summary: The critical path includes multiple render-blocking styles and weak cache/image delivery signals.
findings.evidence: HAR found three parser-inserted very-high-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse failed cache, image-delivery, dependency-tree and render-blocking insights. DOM confirmation shows scripts are deferred, so the issue is concentrated in styles and delivery rather than falsely labelling those scripts blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer route-specific styles, improve cache policy, and tune image discovery/priority.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused and legacy code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed unused CSS, unused JavaScript, and legacy JavaScript audits; HAR recorded 61 scripts and about 1.02 MB transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and interaction, remove legacy output for modern browsers, and defer optional integrations until user intent.

findings.summary: Some controls and links lack usable accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name, label-content-name-mismatch, and list audits; the image primitive also found one image without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair names at the semantic source, align visible and accessible labels, use valid list markup, and give meaningful imagery appropriate alternatives.

findings.summary: Text/UI contrast does not consistently meet WCAG minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed on the sampled homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and control tokens to meet WCAG contrast in every state, then rerun automated and visual checks.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and document structure need repair.
findings.evidence: The focused first link had no outline or shadow, and Lighthouse reported structural/list accessibility failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic landmarks and heading/list structure, preserve logical tab order, and add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring.

findings.summary: Narrow reflow fails and controls fall below recommended target size.
findings.evidence: At 360 px, content remains 1038 px wide with 678 px overflow; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport/target-size and the mobile account panel is mostly beyond the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow true reflow and user scaling, use intrinsic sizing, and enlarge hit areas. Audit video captions separately on each player asset.

findings.summary: Many images omit intrinsic dimensions or are oversized.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 29 of 36 images without width/height and 12 oversized relative to display; Lighthouse failed unsized-images and image-delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every card image and request the smallest appropriate responsive source.

findings.summary: Localized variants are not connected with hreflang metadata.
findings.evidence: The Japanese page links to many language hosts, but the head probe found no link[hreflang]; sitemap.xml returned 404. Canonical and robots were otherwise present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish reciprocal hreflang annotations and a discoverable sitemap index consistent with robots and canonicals.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks structured and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph properties despite a public, indexable content catalogue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate WebSite/Organization JSON-LD and Open Graph metadata that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: CSP is limited to frame-ancestors; X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are absent. Two first-party cookies lack Secure and the settings cookie is SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP beyond frame-ancestors, add nosniff and Referrer-Policy, and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The anonymous homepage has a broad third-party/network footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 118 of 145 requests and 1.62 of 1.74 MB on non-page origins, including Google account code and advertising/CDN origins; trackers inventory found 16 third-party origins. Some are organizational CDNs, but the total cross-origin surface is still large.
findings.suggestedFix: Classify every cross-origin dependency, delay optional advertising/auth/analytics until consent or intent, and batch/minimise telemetry.

findings.summary: Public account entry points do not expose phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: The sampled signup surface advertises email and federated entry; no WebAuthn/passkey capability was exposed in the rendered flow. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside recovery-safe alternatives, requested only from an explicit account action.

findings.summary: Defensive policy coverage is narrow.
findings.evidence: HSTS and clickjacking protection are present, but Referrer-Policy and nosniff are absent; Permissions-Policy only declares two client-hint features, and CSP only supplies frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit least-privilege Permissions-Policy and Referrer-Policy, add nosniff, and expand CSP with script/style/object/base directives and Trusted Types where feasible.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and risks extra layout work.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 12 oversized images, 16 legacy-format URLs, 29 missing dimensions, and 8 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate correctly sized AVIF/WebP candidates, provide srcset/sizes, dimensions, and lazy loading for below-fold imagery.

findings.summary: The initial page executes more script and requests than its listing task needs.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 145 requests and 61 scripts; Lighthouse identified unused CSS/JS and legacy JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Load page-template essentials first and conditionally import account, creator, advertising, and other secondary code after intent.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates transferred bytes before media playback begins.
findings.evidence: Cross-origin resources account for 1.62 MB of the 1.74 MB homepage transfer; script alone is about 1.02 MB before the user starts a video.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template third-party and script budgets, self-host or remove low-value dependencies, and defer media/ads until visible or requested.

taskList.title: Repair focus, names, structure, target size, and contrast
Reduce and conditionally load JavaScript and third parties
Harden CSP, cookies, and browser security policies
Make consent semantic and less obstructive
Optimise responsive image delivery and reserve space
Respect theme, motion, and contrast preferences
Add localized indexing and share metadata
Progressively enhance navigation transitions and positioning
Offer passkeys from account entry points
